drafts.text: The AI trade had a scary week. The buildout didn't. The US now counts 5,159 data centers, operating or in the pipeline, more than the next nine countries combined, per The Kobeissi Letter. Every one needs power, transformers and cooling. That demand doesn't reprice on a Monday.
drafts.video_tip: 15s: map of the US lighting up with data-center dots, a counter running to 5,159, then cut to a substation/transformer shot for the power angle.

drafts.text: Last week markets were pricing a hawkish Fed. Now the New York Fed's Williams calls 2027 a year of lower inflation and blames recent pressure on unusual factors, per First Squawk. Energy shocks push prices up, then they unwind. That unwind is the disinflation.
drafts.video_tip: 10-15s: Williams headline card, then a simple line chart of an energy-price spike rolling over with 'inflation follows' as the caption.

drafts.text: Evercore calls it AI's first bailout, per ZeroHedge, then concedes it isn't a balance-sheet rescue. No balance sheet was rescued. Markets priced continuity at the company supplying the chips for a trillion-dollar buildout. That's a leadership story, not a solvency story.
drafts.video_tip: 10s: split screen with 'BAILOUT?' on the left and 'LEADERSHIP' on the right; strike through the left side as the Evercore quote scrolls.

drafts.text: Bloomberg says the wheels are coming off the AI funding rush, per Unusual Whales. The same day, Nvidia added $955B in market cap, the largest one-day gain by any stock in history, per The Kobeissi Letter. Funding fear is loud. Demand for compute is louder.
drafts.video_tip: 10-15s: the Bloomberg 'wheels coming off' quote fades out, the '+$955B' bar shoots up beside it; end on 'demand for compute'.
